messages.text: Explain bootstrapping for my MSc class tomorrow in a way that doesn't need heavy maths. They know the CLT.

Try this: we usually have only one sample, but we want to know how much a statistic like the mean would wobble if we could sample again. Bootstrapping pretends our sample is the population: we resample from it with replacement thousands of times, compute the statistic each time, and look at the spread. That spread approximates the sampling distribution, without needing a formula.
nice. quick R snippet they can run in the lab?

x <- c(12, 15, 9, 20, 14, 11, 17)
boot_means <- replicate(5000, mean(sample(x, replace = TRUE)))
quantile(boot_means, c(0.025, 0.975))
hist(boot_means)
The quantiles give a 95% percentile interval for the mean.

Ha, the chai can wait half an hour. The snippet above should run as-is in base R; if the lab machines are slow, drop the replicates to 2000.

messages.text: explain vesting cliff like im 5

Imagine you get 48 candies for staying four years, one per month. A cliff means you get nothing for the first 12 months, and then on the one-year anniversary you get 12 candies at once. After that, one candy each month. If you leave before a year, you get zero.

With vesting and a one-year cliff, someone who leaves at six months keeps no vested shares; the company or the other founders can buy back the unvested ones at a nominal price. messages.text: on call and payments-gateway pods keep getting OOMKilled. limits are 512Mi, it's a JVM service. where do i start

Start by checking whether the JVM heap is sized relative to the container limit. On recent JDKs, set -XX:MaxRAMPercentage (for example 70-75) instead of a fixed -Xmx, so the heap leaves room for metaspace, threads and off-heap buffers. Then compare `kubectl top pod` against the limit and look at the pod's last termination reason.

That's very likely the cause: with -Xmx equal to the container limit, any non-heap memory pushes the process over 512Mi and the kernel kills it. Either drop -Xmx to around 360m or switch to MaxRAMPercentage=70, and consider raising the limit to 768Mi if traffic is growing.

I can't give legal advice, but generally a deposit is meant to cover unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear, and routine repainting after a normal tenancy is often treated as wear and tear. messages.text: hey, need help with a hook for my next video. its a blind test, £30 mic vs £300 mic for voiceover. i keep starting with 'hey guys welcome back' and i hate it

Start with the payoff instead of the greeting. Something like: 'One of these mics costs ten times more than the other, and I bet you can't tell which. Let's find out.' You can introduce yourself and the channel after the first reveal. Want a couple more options in different tones?
yeah give me a funny one and a serious one

Funny: 'I spent £300 on a microphone so you don't have to, and honestly my cat sounds the same on both.' Serious: 'Does expensive audio gear actually make you sound better, or are we paying for the box? I ran a blind test to find out.' Both lead into the same reveal, so you can pick whichever matches your usual tone.
funny one is good. now thumbnail text, 3 words max, has to read on a phone screen

A few options: 'CAN YOU HEAR IT?', '£30 vs £300', or 'WHICH IS WHICH?'. Keep the text in a heavy sans-serif with a thick outline, and put it on the opposite side from the two mics so faces and gear stay visible. High-contrast yellow on a dark background tends to survive tiny previews well.

Here you go. 'Can a £30 mic beat a £300 one? I recorded the same script on both and tested it blind. 00:00 Intro, 00:00 The setup, 00:00 Round one: voiceover, 00:00 Round two: noisy room, 00:00 The reveal, 00:00 Verdict.' Add your gear links under the chapters, and put the most important sentence in the first two lines because that's all that shows before 'show more'.

It depends on your timing. Resolve's free version is capable and handles long timelines well, but the learning curve costs a few weeks of slower work. If you're under pressure right now, you could finish the current project where it is and trial Resolve on something small afterwards. Also try clearing the cache and using proxies, which fixes many crashes.

A few: 'Blind Spot', 'Ear Test', 'Sound Check', or 'Gear Gauntlet'. 'Blind Spot' works nicely because the tests are blind and it hints at things people miss. Keep the title card short so it doesn't eat into your hook.

messages.text: quick q. for a willingness-to-pay study is Van Westendorp enough or do I need conjoint? it's for my MSc thesis on what parents in SEA will pay for kids' reading apps

Van Westendorp is fine if your question is the acceptable price range for one product. Conjoint is better when you want to know how much each feature is worth, like live tutoring versus a parent dashboard. For a master's thesis, Van Westendorp plus a few purchase-intent questions is usually defensible, as long as you discuss its limits.
ok good. I have 412 responses but most came from Quillstep's own parent mailing list. my supervisor already flagged that as sampling bias

That's a fair flag: existing users have already shown they'll pay something. You could recruit a comparison sample through an online panel, or at least compare your sample's demographics to census figures and report the gap.

Then make it a clearly argued limitation. Compare demographics to public data, run the analysis separately for paying and non-paying sign-ups if you have both, and avoid generalising to all parents in the region.

A lot of founders hear that. Keeping the thesis tightly scoped is the best answer to it: fewer methods, a clear question, and a realistic writing plan.

messages.text: on call and payments-gateway pods keep getting OOMKilled. limits are 512Mi, it's a JVM service. where do i start

Start by checking whether the JVM heap is sized relative to the container limit. On recent JDKs, set -XX:MaxRAMPercentage (for example 70-75) instead of a fixed -Xmx, so the heap leaves room for metaspace, threads and off-heap buffers. Then compare `kubectl top pod` against the limit and look at the pod's last termination reason.
MaxRAMPercentage isn't set at all lol. Xmx is hardcoded to 512m

That's very likely the cause: with -Xmx equal to the container limit, any non-heap memory pushes the process over 512Mi and the kernel kills it. Either drop -Xmx to around 360m or switch to MaxRAMPercentage=70, and consider raising the limit to 768Mi if traffic is growing.

Cost of equity woh return hai jo shareholders apne paise par expect karte hain, jabke WACC poori company ka blended cost hai: equity aur debt dono ko unke weights ke hisaab se mila kar. Happy to help. A tighter version: 'Hospital wastewater is a major reservoir of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, but its spread into the community is poorly understood. We characterised effluent isolates and compared their resistance profiles.' To reach 250 words overall, cut the background sentences and keep one line each on methods, results and implications. Want me to go through the rest paragraph by paragraph?

That error usually means the object name doesn't exist in your session. Check with ls() whether your data frame is really called df; if you loaded it with read.csv into another name, use that name inside ggplot(). It's also worth checking the column names with names().

Please don't paste API keys into chats; treat that one as exposed and regenerate it in your NCBI account settings. The most common cause of failures is the rate limit: without a key you get 3 requests per second, with one you get 10, so add a short sleep between calls and load the key from an environment variable instead of the script.
